case_title: Bhola Nath and Anr. v. State
fact_summary:
The present appeal was filed before High Court of Uttarakhand against conviction of the 2 accused, Bhola Nath and Meera in a Sessions Trial. Both the accused were convicted under Section 363, 368, 372/511 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, IPC) and sentenced to undergo RI for two and half years along with a fine of Rs. 1000/- each under Section 372/511 IPC and in default, to undergo three months additional RI. Each of the accused were also sentenced to undergo RI for two years along with fine of Rs. 500/- each under Section 363 & 368 IPC and in default, to undergo two months additional RI.

Briefly stated in June 1996, the police received information through their informer (mukhbir) that the accused were dealing in buying and selling of minor children. The police found the two accused along with two minor girls (14 and 11 years) and one minor boy (13 years). The children told the police that the appellants accused had taken them for the purpose of sale. Subsequent to the police investigation the matter was committed to trial. After appreciating the evidence available on record, the Additional Sessions Judge, Haridwar vide judgment and order dated 15.5.1998 convicted and sentenced the accused appellants as mentioned above.

The High Court in the appeal, examined the basis of the prosecution case. The two minor victim girls who were sisters, mentioned that the accused took them under the pretext of reuniting them with their parents, but tried to sell them for Rs. 30,000/-. At the time of aforesaid incident, many people collected at the place of occurrence and after seeing the crowd the police also reached there and caught the appellants accused. To prove its case, the prosecution examined the two female victims, police personnel, eye witnesses of recovery, and the Investigating Officer. However, the accused whilst denying the allegations did not produce any documentary or oral evidence in their defence.

The High Court rejected the appeal of the appellant accused and upheld the conviction and sentence on the following grounds:

i) That the prosecution, to prove its case, has examined eight witnesses including the victims, the public witnesses and the witness of recovery. All these witnesses have supported the prosecution story.

ii) The victim - witness was cross-examined at length but nothing came out which may create any doubt about her testimony.

iii) The statement of the victim - witness was corroborated by statements of police and independent witnesses.

In the present case, the defendants were accused of recruiting five Brazilian women and transferring them to Germany for the purpose of sexual exploitation. The defendants were responsible for recruiting and providing all the documents and tickets for the transfer. The victims were contracted to dance in show clubs; however, when they arrived to Europe they were forced to prostitute in order to pay for their travel expenses.

As reported by the defendants, they were not aware that the women recruited would be prostituted in Germany. As far as they knew, the victims were contracted for dancing in a show club.

The defendant is accused of promoting and facilitating the international departure of two women for sexual exploitation in Spain and of practicing the tentative crime of international trafficking of people for sexual exploitation women (article 231, caput of the Penal Code). According to the accusation, the defendant was assisted by Sergio Gonçalves within the national territory and by his brother that would receive the victims in Spain.

The victims testified that the defendant offered them the trip to Spain, bought their international travel tickets and dollars, expedited all the necessary measures to insure the trip and indicated who would receive them abroad.

In the 1st Instance Court, the defendant was convicted to 3 years and 9 months of imprisonment, converted to 2 penalties restrictive of rights, for two tentative crimes of international trafficking of people for sexual exploitation (article 231, caput of the Penal Code).

The defendant appealed to the 2nd Instance Court, alleging that the crime had prescribed and that the accusation of the practice of the tentative crime of international trafficking of people for sexual exploitation (article 231, caput of the Penal Code) was not a valid accusation since the departure from the national territory was not consumed due to the police intervention upon boarding the victims and that the victims knew that they would travel abroad to practice prostitution.

The 2nd Instance Court denied the appeal, affirming that the crime of international trafficking of people for sexual exploitation (article 231, caput of the Penal Code) did not prescribe, that it is not necessary to have completed all the acts of the crime to characterize the tentative of its commitment and that the crime is characterized when all the measures needed to facilitate and promote the victim`s departure from the country are taken, even if the victims knew that they would travel abroad to practice prostitution.

The defendant, LEONILSON JOSE TENORIO MADRUGA, was accused of attempted human trafficking for recruiting and promoting the exit of two Brazilian women from Brazil to Spain to exercise prostitution abroad. On 03/08/1999, LEONILSON was arrested in the International Airport of Guararapes while the victims were about to board their plane to Spain. Along with co-defendant SÉRGIO GONÇALVES MARIANO, LEONILSON bought their plane tickets and gave them money.

On 16 September 1997, the defendant Lee Chien Mao was arrested in flagrant delicto, at a flight from Brazil to China, while tried to promote the output of the victims E.M. and L.V.V. for the purpose of sexual exploitation in Taipe, Taiwan.The defendant recruited the victims E.M. and L.V.V, who by the time of the facts were minors, to work as prostitutes in Taiwan, promising them 3,000 dollars per month.The defendant cooperated with Guinalva Adriane Alves dos Santos who was the manager of a prostitution agency in Caxias do Sul, Brazil. It was this place where false documents, photos of naked women and pornographic material were found. At the same place, Guinalva intermediated sexual encounters and harboured a lot of minors. It is important to say that the process was dismembered in relation to the defendant Guinalva Adriane Alves dos Santos.

Between September 1994 and mid-1995 the defendants jointly tried to promote the sending of the newborn K. C. S. abroad without legal formalities and by profit, hoping that the child will be adopted by the French couple Q. L. C. and N. E. B. C. Therefore, Marluce Mercês was hired by the French couple, through the intermediate of D.N., upon payment of $ 7,500.00 (seven thousand five hundred U.S. dollars), which U.S. $ 4,000.00 (four thousand) were paid at first and the rest later in the act, the amount requested under the pretext of paying court costs. D. and Marluce, however, disappeared with the money received and not resolved the issue alluding to adoption. Therefore, the imputation was performed in relation to them also the crime of embezzlement. Before, however, Marluce started the lawsuit for adoption in the district of Palmares / PE. After, she did an identical action in the District of Piranhas / AL. Marluce and Manoel Ronildo took the child and his mother, R. C. S., to the municipality of São José da Tapera / AL, where effected a false record of birth, and in which it declared that the child was born in Alagoas and in which the very Manoel Ronildo served as witness. Marluce took the newborn and his mother to the home of a friend of co-defendant Manoel Ronildo that, at his request, welcomed both during the entire period in which the action was processed in Alagoas. Already on 01/26/1995, Marluce Mercês and Ramiro de Souza Ferreira led the minor and his mother to the Civil Registry Office of Palmares, where new birth certificate was issued. This time, the child was named G. K. C. S. Ramiro was responsible for transporting the child and his mother between Palmares / PE and São José da Tapera / AL. He himself, even before the birth of the child, he assumed to the mother that he had the commitment to give the child for adoption.

She was provided with a false ID and on January 17, 2008, taken by car from Ostrava to a brothel called Villa Rouge in St. Valentin, Austria. From there A. H. was taken another brothel called Big Ben. After A. H. refused prostitution, she was made to by threats and beating. Consequently she was moved to brothel called Saphir in Ulmerfeld – Hausmening. The money earned by prostitution was taken from here, until she was found by Austrian Police on March 3, 2008.

Defendants offered and organised voluntary prostitution of G. Á. in brothel called Le Souterrain in Vienna. G. A. paid 60 % of her profits for that arrangement.

Defendants organised voluntary prostitution of S. C. in bed and breakfast called Eva in Ostrava-Radvanice, Czech Republic. S. C. paid 30 % of her profits for that arrangement plus 500 CZK for every day that she offered prostitution in the bed and breakfast.

The Coastguard authority looked for the victim and they found her in the company of the accused.

The defendant was accused of maintaining a house of prostitution and favoring prostitution, accusations that where discharged. The first accusation was discharged in virtue of legal doctrine and jurisprudence that orient that the crime foreseen in article 229 of the Penal Code be discharged in view of the social adaptation and acceptance to this conduct. The accusation of favoring prostitution was not proven, reason for which it was also discharged. The defendant was also accused of domestic trafficking in persons, conduct that was not confirmed by the alleged victims which led to acquittal for this crime. As for the crime of submission of an under aged victim to prostitution, the defendant was convicted in the first instance. The crimes of ruffianism, false identity and providing alcohol to a minor were not proven, therefore they were discharged. The defendant was condemned to 5 years and 4 moths of imprisonment, in a closed prison regime and 17 daily fines. The Court of Appeals reduced the penalty to 3 years and 6 months of imprisonment and 11 daily fines, and maintained the rest of the initial verdict.

The defendants argue that they never met the victims nor did they provide any money for the victim’s travel expenses. One of these trafficked women was apparently a teenager. The accused were two men, DIRLEI DE OLIVEIRA and JOSÉ ARTEMÉDIO PEREIRA, and a Paraguayan woman, GLORIS MARLENE MERELES. It is worth remarking that this criminal process was only brought against JORGE RICARDO DE SOUZA REIS.

The defendants operated night club Scandaleux in Znojmo, Oblekovice 37. They have entered with the underage girls into an oral agreement that the girls can voluntarily practice prostitution in the club and that they will share their profits with the defendants. Upon arrival to Paris, C.S. was received by the defendant R.J.L. who took her to the apartment where he was living. Two days after, the defendant forced her to work as a prostitute. Utterly dissatisfied with the situation she was submitted to, the victim went back to Brazil using a flight ticket she had hidden.

It is important to say that the process was dismembered in relation to the defendant R.J.L., as he was living in France at an unknown location.
